chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad, may Allah have mercy upon him, narrated from al-Mufaddhal who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, created the believers from a single origin. No one enters them who is not of them, and no one leaves them who is of them. Their example, by Allah, is like the head for the body and the fingers for the hand. So whoever you see differs from that, testify against him decisively that he is a hypocrite.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual nature and unity of believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Sifat al-Shia*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the essential characteristic of the true Shia as an indivisible spiritual unity, organic unity, likening them to the head and fingers of a single hand to emphasize their inseparable connection. He establishes a clear criterion for distinguishing the faithful from the hypocrites (*munafiqun*), asserting that any deviation from this cohesive state serves as definitive proof of hypocrisy. This concept underscores the Shia understanding of *wilayah* and communal identity as a singular, cohesive entity rather than a loose association of individuals.
